block: Twenty-three of thirty-two board packets can never reach CPM/PERT allocation, because this board has never declared a readiness policy and the bulk-ready verb refuses by design rather than inferring one

impact_if_unanswered: The rebalance you asked for can only ever draw on the 2 ready packets, the 23 backlog packets stay invisible to dispatch indefinitely, and every future takt and burndown reading on this board keeps reporting a famine whose cause is one undeclared boolean.

options.consequence: Newly ingested packets land ready and bulk-ready becomes usable, so the 23 backlog packets can be moved into the dispatch pool in one operator-invoked command and the CPM/PERT rebalance finally has real supply; it also means future ingests skip a human readiness check, so a badly-minted packet reaches the ready column without review.

decision.rationale: Engineer ruling 2026-09-01: declare ingest_ready_default true on the glpnet board. 23 days of total dispatch famine on 23 packets outweighs the risk of a badly-minted packet reaching ready, which the claim step already gates; reversible in one edit.

block: The two live release-bar rulings still contradict each other and will collide again next cut, even though today's instance was settled by fact when a peer cut v2026-09-01-1 mid-session
background: Ruling Q-GLPNETA13-01 at 2026-08-31T13:44Z answered 'Feature-level bar' — a release needs a completed, fully-implemented, codex-reviewed FEATURE.

options.label: Retire the feature-level bar, content bar governs

options.label: Retire the content bar, feature bar governs

block: Similar-size non-overlapping work packages cannot be achieved by re-allocating the current packets, because 22 of the 25 are individually larger than a whole day of capacity
background: Measured 2026-09-01T08:35Z after the readiness policy was declared: buildkit-scheduler cycle now allocates across all four hosts — ariellas 7 WPs 376h, gavriella 6 WPs 328h, olamnit 6 WPs 248h, shiras 6 WPs 320h.

impact_if_unanswered: Every future cycle on this board produces a plan that defers on day one regardless of how the work is split between hosts, and the per-host allocation reads as a schedule while being a list of things nothing can start.

options.label: Split packets to at or under the daily cap
options.consequence: The 22 oversized packets are re-minted as sub-packets of 24 hours or less so the allocator can actually place them, which is the only change that makes the per-host split executable rather than uniformly deferred; it costs a re-ingest pass over 22 packets and every existing claim and dependency edge has to be carried onto the sub-packets.

recommendation.because: The deferral is structural rather than contention — no amount of re-allocation moves an 80 hour packet under a 24 hour cap — so every other option leaves the plan deferring on day one, and raising the cap buys a green board by making the calendar lie.

decision.rationale: Engineer ruling 2026-09-01: split the 22 oversized packets to at-or-under the 24h daily slot cap. Raising the cap would make the calendar lie; accepting deferral forecloses same-day dispatch permanently.

block: Every CPM/PERT number this board has ever produced is sized against a 24-hour working day, and only you can declare what this host's real working day is
background: Peer broadcast from gavriella/yngraw at 2026-09-01T09:00Z root-caused it by a different method on a different board: buildkit-scheduler onboard --shifts declares a CONTINUOUS 3x8h shift calendar, which tiles the day completely at 00:00, 08:00 and 16:00 and therefore means 24h per day by design.

Corroborated here independently: this board reports ariellas capacity=86400s and capacity_horizon=432000s over 5 days — exactly 24h per day — and identical values across six independently onboarded actors, which is the signature of a constant rather than a measurement.
That broadcast records engineer ruling Q-CAPACITY-01: allocations stay computed-but-unconfirmed until each host re-declares real capacity and the cycle is re-run.

It also warns explicitly that the fix must NOT substitute a different hardcoded constant, because capacity is a declared input and baking in 8h reproduces the fallback-used-is-a-literal-true defect one layer up.

Verified in the buildkit source: onboard --window is action=append so a whole horizon can be declared in ONE call, and all windows in one call share a report_id whose derivation supersedes the earlier shift report rather than adding to it.
Consequence for the allocation this lane published at 08:40Z: it was computed against a 24h budget, so every day-full deferral in it is measured against a budget that may be three times too large.
impact_if_unanswered: This host keeps a 24h working day, the allocation published at 08:40Z stays unconfirmable under Q-CAPACITY-01, and every packet-splitting target derived from the daily cap in Q-GLPNETA16-08 is derived from a number nobody declared.

options.label: Declare one 8h working window per day
options.consequence: One 08:00-16:00Z window per day is declared for the 120-day horizon in a single onboard call that supersedes the shift calendar, giving a conventional working day and roughly a third of the current budget; it is a declaration this lane makes on your behalf, so if your intended day is longer the board under-allocates instead of over-allocating.

options.label: Declare one 12h working window per day
options.consequence: One 08:00-20:00Z window per day is declared, halving the current budget rather than cutting it to a third and matching a long-session lane that runs well beyond office hours; it still over-states any day on which the lane is not actually attended for twelve hours.

options.label: Keep the 24h calendar as a deliberate declaration
options.consequence: The board is declared to be a continuously-attended automation host where a 24h day is honest, and no re-onboarding happens; this forecloses comparability with every peer host that re-declares a real working day under Q-CAPACITY-01, and forecloses using this board's P50/P80/P95 dates as commitments against human availability.

recommendation.because: It is the value the peer broadcast measured as the real day behind the 3x8h tiling and the one every other host is being asked to adopt, so it makes this board's numbers comparable fleet-wide today; it is one command to change if your intended day is longer, whereas keeping 24h leaves this lane the only host whose dates mean something different from everyone else's.

decision.rationale: Engineer ruling 2026-09-01: ARIELLAS glpnet is DECLARED a continuously-attended automation host, so 24h/day is an honest declaration here and no re-onboard happens. Discharges Q-CAPACITY-01 for this board by explicit declaration rather than re-measurement. Accepts the stated foreclosure: this board's P50/P80/P95 are not commitments against human availability and are not directly comparable with peer hosts that declare a working day.
